newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Deutsche issues call warrants on Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche issues call warrants on Telecom.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG on Tuesday announced an issue of call warrants over ordinary shares in Telecom Corporation of New Zealand.
Garlick and Co Ltd is broker to the issue.

The Telecom call warrants are similar to call options, giving holders the right but not the obligation to buy shares in Telecom from Deutsche Bank at any time before the expiry date, at a price determined when the warrants are issued.
The warrants, which expire on September 23, 1998, allow investors to buy one Telecom share for every two warrants exercised at a cost of NZ$7.60 per share.

The issue price will vary depending on the performance of Telecom shares. The market price of the warrant will be affected by a number of factors, including the price of Telecom shares, the time remaining until the warrants expire, and the volatility of Telecom's share price.

Robert Gipslis of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Securities, the global coordinator for the issue, said the warrants could be traded on the stock exchange like any other shares, so investors could buy or sell at any time.
"You pay only a fraction of the share price to buy the warrant, but the change in the warrant price is a lot steeper than the change in the share price," he said.
Bill Garlick, managing director of Garlick and Co, said warrants provided leverage to take advantage of the upside.
"The other advantage is that the leverage you get from the warrant has limited risk -- you can't lose more than what you pay for the warrant," he said.
Applications for the warrant will be accepted from February 17, and trading on the New Zealand Stock Exchange will start on March 3.
Almost one billion Deutsche Bank-issued warrants were traded in Australia in 1996.
